title: Cross-org user cannot join another organization's project room even with a validly-signed JWT
description: join-project-room compares the target Project's organizationId to socket.orgId, which is derived exclusively from the verified JWT during the io.use auth middleware — the client-supplied organizationId in the connection auth payload is never trusted for this check.
preconditions: Valid JWT issued for a real user belonging to Org B
steps: Connect to Socket.IO with a valid Org B JWT
Emit join-project-room with { projectId: P._id } (Org A's project)
expectedResult: Server responds with 'project-room-join-denied'; the socket is never added to room project:{P._id}; no scan-progress or scan-completed event for Org A's project is ever delivered to this socket.

title: Same-org user who is not a project member cannot join that project's room
description: The T24 hardening upgrades the org-match check to a full project-membership check via computeProjectAccessForUser(); a user in the correct org but not assigned to the project (and not a project.admin) is denied.
preconditions: Project P belongs to Org A
A user in Org A who is NOT assigned to P and does not hold project.admin
steps: Connect to Socket.IO as this Org A, non-member user
expectedResult: Server responds 'project-room-join-denied' — same-org membership alone is insufficient; the user must be an explicit project member or project admin to receive P's live scan events.

title: GET /notifications/client and /notifications/unread-count ignore any client-supplied organization identifier and use only the JWT-derived req.orgId
description: Both handlers pass req.orgId (set by the authenticate middleware from the verified token) directly into the Mongo filter; there is no organizationId read from query/body, so a forged query param cannot widen the scope.
preconditions: Valid JWT for a user in Org A
Notifications exist for the same user under a differently-scoped record in Org B (data anomaly / test fixture)
steps: As the Org A user, call GET /notifications/client?organizationId={OrgB_id} and GET /notifications/unread-count?organizationId={OrgB_id}
expectedResult: The forged organizationId query parameter is ignored; results are scoped strictly to req.orgId (Org A) from the JWT — no Org B notification data or count is returned.

title: Internal notification endpoint fails closed (503) when INTERNAL_API_TOKEN is unconfigured, rather than accepting any request
description: internalAuth() checks !INTERNAL_TOKEN first and returns 503 before any comparison. This must never fall through to allowing unauthenticated dispatch just because the env var is missing in a given deployment.
preconditions: A test deployment/config with both INTERNAL_API_TOKEN and INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN unset
steps: POST /api/internal/notifications with no X-Internal-Token header and a fully valid body
expectedResult: 503 'Internal endpoint not configured' — no notification is created, confirming the endpoint fails closed rather than open when unconfigured.

title: Internal endpoint token comparison uses timing-safe equality and length pre-check without leaking token length via response timing
preconditions: INTERNAL_API_TOKEN configured to a known long value in a test environment
steps: Send repeated POST /api/internal/notifications requests with X-Internal-Token values of varying lengths and varying prefix-match lengths against the real token
Statistically compare response latency across attempts
expectedResult: crypto.timingSafeEqual combined with the explicit a.length !== b.length short-circuit means observable response timing does not meaningfully correlate with how many leading bytes of the guessed token were correct — no practical timing side channel for brute-forcing the token byte-by-byte.

title: Socket.IO connection is rejected pre-handshake completion when no auth token is supplied
steps: Attempt to connect a Socket.IO client with no `auth.token` field set
expectedResult: The io.use() middleware calls next(new Error('No token provided')); the connection is refused and no 'connection' event fires for this socket, so it can join no rooms and receive no notifications or scan events.

title: DEV_BYPASS cannot enable the Socket.IO auth bypass in a production environment
description: core/socket.js computes DEV_BYPASS = process.env.DEV_BYPASS === 'true' && process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' at module load — the NODE_ENV guard must prevent the bypass (which assigns every socket the same DEV_ORG_ID and skips JWT verification) from ever activating in production regardless of how DEV_BYPASS is set.
preconditions: A build/runtime configured with NODE_ENV=production and DEV_BYPASS=true set simultaneously (misconfiguration scenario)
steps: Start the backend with NODE_ENV=production and DEV_BYPASS=true
Attempt to connect a Socket.IO client with no token, or with an invalid token
expectedResult: The connection is still rejected with a JWT verification error — DEV_BYPASS has no effect because NODE_ENV==='production', confirming the bypass cannot be accidentally left on in a production deployment.

title: An authenticated user cannot mark-read or delete another user's notification by guessing/enumerating its ObjectId
description: Both markRead and deleteOne filter on { _id, targetUserId: String(userId) }; a syntactically valid ObjectId belonging to a different user's notification simply matches zero documents.
preconditions: Notification N belongs to User A
Valid JWT for unrelated User C
expectedResult: Both calls fail to affect N (404 on read, silent no-op on delete since deleteOne's filter matches nothing) — N remains unread and undeleted for User A.
